request.goal: Extend src/platform.ts with an exported safeWindowsFileName(name) that renames a reserved Windows device name so it can be created on Windows. Acceptance requires observing on Windows that the returned name can actually be created and the original cannot.

plan.summary: Export safeWindowsFileName from src/platform.ts so reserved Windows device names are remapped to names that can be created as files on Windows.
plan.overview: Reuse isReservedDeviceName to detect CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9 and prefix those names so they are no longer reserved; leave other names unchanged. Add src/platform.test.ts for remap checks plus a Windows-only file-create observation. This Linux host cannot observe reserved-device create/fail behavior, so that named case is extra evidence on win32.

features.title: Export safeWindowsFileName
features.summary: Add exported safeWindowsFileName that remaps reserved Windows device names via isReservedDeviceName so the returned name can be created as a file on Windows while the original cannot.
validation: safeWindowsFileName remaps reserved names and leaves others unchanged
Named case: safeWindowsFileName returned name can be created on Windows when the original reserved name cannot

requirements: Export safeWindowsFileName(name: string): string from src/platform.ts
Reserved Windows device names are renamed so they are not reserved
On Windows, creating a file with the original reserved name fails and creating a file with the returned name succeeds
Non-goal: changing isReservedDeviceName matching, drive-letter handling, or POSIX filename sanitization
decisions: Prefix reserved names with _ (for example CON becomes _CON) using existing isReservedDeviceName
Windows file-creation acceptance is extra evidence on win32 because this Linux host cannot observe reserved device names
Gate remains bun test; the named Windows case uses skipIf on non-win32
Add src/platform.test.ts for always-on remap checks and the Windows create observation
